title: Derived Artifacts: Recompute From the Tree, Verify at the Merge

intelligence.essence: Never verify a derived artifact against the change that produced it: recompute it from the live target tree at a named pin (SN-0238, SN-0216), compare semantically so a volatile timestamp is not a difference (SN-0217), generate only on a clean worktree at the exact committed tree the artifact must describe (SN-0327), and re-verify at the merge commit itself, because the merge creates a new tree that pre-merge proof does not transfer to (SN-0328).
intelligence.human_view: An index or a generated list is only as good as the last time someone rebuilt it from the real files and compared. You never check the list against the paperwork that created it — you recount from the shelf. If the only difference is a timestamp stamp, it's the same item, not a change. And you never take the count from a messy desk: clean tree first, then count.
intelligence.child_view: It's like counting your crayons. You don't trust yesterday's list — you dump the box and count again. And the counter only counts the crayons already in the box — if a new crayon is still in your pocket, the list misses it and still says "all good." And if a crayon just has a new sticker on it, it's still the same crayon.
intelligence.grandma_view: A pantry inventory written from memory will always be wrong, dear. You open the cupboards and count what's actually there. A jar with a new label is still the same jar of jam. And the count only ever sees what's actually been put away — the counter reads the shelf, not the bags still on the floor — so a jar that hasn't been shelved yet never makes the list at all.
intelligence.ai_view: For any derived artifact: recompute from `git ls-tree`/contents at the target ref; exclude self-referential entries by design and say so; normalize volatile stamps before diffing; refuse to generate from a dirty worktree; after any merge touching the artifact, regenerate at the merge commit and compare. Show the check failing without the repair whenever you claim a repair — a one-directional proof is half a proof.
intelligence.what_it_means: Six notes, one principle with four working edges: recompute-at-target, semantic identity, clean-tree generation, merge-commit re-verification. Every stale-index incident in this family was the same failure wearing a different hat — somebody trusted a projection instead of the tree. The tree is the truth; everything derived is a claim about it that must be re-derivable on demand.
whats_inside: Verification of a derived artifact recomputes it from the live target tree at a named pin; the producing change's own blobs are never the evidence (SN-0238, SN-0216).
Producers regenerate in their landing step; consumers never patch a derived number by hand (SN-0213).
Drift comparison is semantic: volatile provenance stamps are not differences (SN-0217).
Regeneration reads the committed tree: the worktree must be clean and HEAD the exact commit the artifact must describe, or the output is a check-green index of the wrong tree (SN-0327).
Merges touching derived artifacts re-verify at the merge commit — the merge is a new tree, and pre-merge proof does not transfer to it (SN-0328).
